purpose: Assess whether a BoE-specific mediated labour channel can be reconstructed point-in-time without revised-history substitution.
reaction_function: Labour tightness -> wages -> services/domestic inflation -> BoE reaction -> front-end rates -> GBP

labour.source: ONS A01 vintage archive already certified in project

average_weekly_earnings.evidence: ONS dataset page explicitly exposes previous dataset versions and explains scheduled revisions; archived files are timestamped by superseded/release dates.
average_weekly_earnings.pit_implication: Strong candidate for vintage reconstruction using archived monthly dataset files rather than current revised history.

cpi_services.evidence: ONS time-series page exposes View previous versions; current series is monthly and has explicit release dates.
cpi_services.pit_implication: Candidate for first-known monthly services-inflation vintages.

front_end.preferred_curve: Sterling OIS daily archive for policy-expectations confirmation; nominal government curve may be retained as secondary same-basis rates layer.
front_end.evidence: BoE publishes daily archive yield curves including sterling overnight index swap curves; nominal government curves are available daily from 1979.
front_end.pit_implication: A same-basis front-end confirmation layer is structurally feasible.

materialization_plan: 1. Reconstruct monthly AWE vintage table from ONS previous-version files, preserving first-known values and release timestamps.
2. Reconstruct CPI services D7NN first-known monthly vintages from ONS previous versions.
3. Materialize a fixed front-end tenor from BoE sterling OIS archive on a single consistent basis.
4. Run diagnostic only: direct labour vs wages/services mediated vs mediated+front-end confirmation, no threshold tuning.
5. Apply chronological walk-forward and robustness before any engine proposal.
guardrails: No current-series retrofill where vintage files exist.
No mixing gilt and OIS rates inside one confirmation series.
No engine/rule changes before OOS evidence.
No inference that BoE equals ECB; only the mediated labour structure is shared, with bank-specific data and rates.
